Case_17023/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2: Violaceous hyperplastic lesions seen on the hard palate

description.short_caption: Violaceous hyperplastic lesions visible on the hard palate.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the oral cavity with a focus on the hard palate. Multiple violaceous, hyperplastic lesions are visible on the hard palate, with some areas appearing nodular or raised. The surrounding mucosa appears intact, and the lesions are localized without obvious ulceration. Teeth and tongue are also visible, providing anatomical context.
visible_findings: violaceous hyperplastic lesions on the hard palate

Case_17023/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Figure 3: Chest CT (without contrast) demonstrated extensive bilateral axillary/hilar/pericardial/mediastinal/porta hepatis lymphadenopathy with associated compression of bronchi, large bilateral pleural effusions and bilateral central consolidation

description.short_caption: Chest CT shows bilateral pleural effusions, central consolidation, and lymphadenopathy.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT image (without contrast) demonstrates extensive bilateral pleural effusions, visible as fluid collections in the pleural spaces. There is significant bilateral central consolidation, particularly in the lower lobes, consistent with dense opacification. Enlarged lymph nodes are evident in the mediastinal and hilar regions, suggesting lymphadenopathy. Compression of adjacent bronchi is also apparent. The image is grayscale with clear delineation of anatomical structures.

Case_17023/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Figure 4: Bronchoscopy image showed a raised purple lesion on the bronchial mucosa

description.short_caption: Bronchoscopy reveals a raised purple lesion on the bronchial mucosa.
description.detailed_description: This bronchoscopy image shows the bronchial mucosa with a raised lesion circled in yellow. The lesion appears purple and irregular, contrasting with the surrounding mucosa, which is smooth and reddish. The lighting and magnification are typical of endoscopic imaging, allowing detailed visualization of the mucosal surface.

Case_17023/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Anti-HHV8 stain of inguinal lymph node showed the typical strong, nuclear but granular staining. (1000x)

description.short_caption: Anti-HHV8 stain of inguinal lymph node showing strong nuclear granular staining.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a high-power view (1000x magnification) of an inguinal lymph node stained with an anti-HHV8 immunohistochemical stain. The stain highlights several nuclei with strong, granular, brown staining against a blue counterstained background. The findings are consistent with HHV8-positive cells, which are often seen in conditions such as Kaposi sarcoma or HHV8-associated lymphoproliferative disorders.

Case_17023/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Bluish/violaceous, hard, firm and nodular lesions seen on his a) left arm and b) left leg

description.short_caption: Bluish, firm nodular lesions on the left arm and left leg.
description.detailed_description: This image shows two separate views of bluish to violaceous nodular lesions. Panel A depicts a single lesion on the left arm, while Panel B shows three similar lesions on the left leg. The lesions appear firm and raised, with a smooth surface. The surrounding skin appears unremarkable without significant erythema or swelling. The lesions are consistent with subcutaneous or dermal processes.

Case_17023/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Inguinal lymph node, core needle biopsy (H&E, 400X). There were abundant macrophages seen within an atypical lymphoid background. The vascular lesion was consistent with KS – seen as intertwined, and proliferating vascular spaces (shown with thickened endothelial lining) and stained positive for CD31.

description.short_caption: Histopathology of inguinal lymph node showing vascular proliferation and atypical lymphoid background (H&E, 400X).
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a core needle biopsy of an inguinal lymph node stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) at 400X magnification. The tissue demonstrates abundant macrophages within an atypical lymphoid background. Proliferating vascular spaces with thickened endothelial linings are evident, consistent with a vascular lesion such as Kaposi sarcoma. The intertwined vascular structures are prominent, and the overall architecture suggests a pathologic process.
